title: Senior Technician
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking a Drive Unit Test Technician! You'll play a hands-on role in advancing next-generation rotating equipment and drive systems. In this fast-paced lab environment, you will perform detailed inspections, install and test drive units on dynamometers, and work closely with engineers to validate performance, reliability, and durability. You will help troubleshoot complex electromechanical challenges, build and modify test fixtures, and maintain a high level of organization and safety in the lab. If you are a mechanically skilled, detail-oriented problem solver with a passion for hands-on engineering work, and are open to supporting testing operations in the Bay Area, this role offers the opportunity to directly influence cutting-edge product development.



What You Will Do 

 - Perform both visual and functional evaluations of rotating equipment
   (motor/engine) and related components to identify defects, inconsistencies,
   and areas for improvement

 - Install drive units onto Dynamometers, conduct testing, and assess
   prototype performance to confirm design assumptions and highlight
   process improvement opportunities

 - Partner with test engineers to develop and execute test procedures, plans,
   and methodologies for verifying drive unit functionality, reliability and
   durability.

 - Coordinate with cross-functional teams —design, reliability, and testing—to
   troubleshoot technical challenges and contribute to design refinement

 - Document test result, inspection reports, and technical observations clearly
   and thoroughly to support informed engineering decisions

 - Maintain a high standard of organization and safety in the lab, including
   inventory, tooling, and equipment maintenance

 - Design, fabricate, and modify test fixtures and equipment to support drive
   system testing and validation

 - Be open to travel to support testing operations in the Bay Area



What You Will Bring 

 - High school diploma or GED required; hands-on technical training or
   certification in automotive, electrical, or similar fields is a plus

 - Strong hands-on background in a comparable role, with a deep
   understanding of engineering concepts and applications

 - Skilled in mechanical assembly and fabrication, with proficiency in
   machine shop tools and expert use of hand/power tools
    1000V HV awareness

 - Capable of independently disassembling and reassembling
   electromechanical assemblies

 - Comfortable using standard lab instruments such as multimeters, DAQ
   systems, and power supplies

 - Experience with wiring harness design and fabrication, including
   soldering, crimping, and following wiring diagrams

 - Strong understanding of physics and engineering fundamentals, with the
   ability to apply principles to solve complex problems

 - Excellent documentation and written communication skills, with
   proficiency in Microsoft Office

 - Exposure to LabVIEW, Python, or equivalent is a plus

 - Ability to lift up to 50 lbs., with frequent standing, walking, and bending in
   a fast-paced lab environment



The pay for this position ranges from $45.00 to $60.00 per hour, depending on experience and qualifications.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

In this role, you will be a member of Also’s Technical Program Management team, responsible for driving the drive unit and actuator modules end to end from concept/proto development phase through mass production. You will partner with product, mechanical, electrical, firmware, test, supply chain, industrial design, and other cross-functional teams to drive product development in consumer-facing products.



What You Will Do 

 - As a Technical Program Manager, you’ll use your product development expertise to lead multi-disciplinary hardware projects from start to finish: managing drive unit programs from architecture and prototyping through validation, industrialization and production ramp.

 - You’ll work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify and manage risks early leading to rapid reaction plans to keep the program on track, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company.

 - Drive the planning and implementation of customer features with the cross-functional teams to hit roadmap goals, tracking progress, while communicating status, blockers, and risks to leadership.

 - Develop and manage comprehensive program schedules via Gantt charts, technical issues, design release management, certification, manufacturing, and resource needs with engineering, supply chain, and cross-functional teams.

 - Identify and solve the top program blockers and adapt lean processes to the organization.



What You Will Bring 

 - Bachelor’s degree in mechanical, or a related engineering field

 - 7+ years of experience in program management, engineering or similar cross-functional role

 - Demonstrated success in shipping drive unit and actuator products from initial concept through mass production.

 - Familiarity with New Product Introduction (NPI) processes, including tooling qualification, PPAP, DVT/PVT, and first-article inspections.

 - Experience managing programs involving electromechanical systems with multiple interdependent subsystems (motors, PCBAs, sensors, structural assemblies).

 - Experience working directly with contract manufacturers and global suppliers on industrialization and production readiness.

 - Ability to understand technical discussions (driven by curiosity to understand how the entire system works) and provide decision framework to make technical decisions and accelerate development.

 - Clear communicator - able to hold conversations with engineering and supply chain while distilling status and decisions for executive leadership.

 - Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (estimated ~10-15%)



The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $250,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.

title: Senior Manager, IT SOX Compliance
description:
The Opportunity
Adobe’s Risk Advisory & Assurance Services (RAAS) team is seeking a Senior Manager to lead our IT SOX compliance program and ensure the technology controls supporting financial reporting are well-designed, effective, and scalable.
This role requires deep expertise in IT SOX and IT general controls, including SAP and cloud environments, along with a solid grasp of enterprise systems, data flows, and end-to-end business processes.
Partnering with the Senior Director, RAAS, you will manage the IT SOX program. You will engage with IT, Finance, control owners, co-sourced testing providers, and external auditors to ensure the program remains efficient and effective.
How You Will Make an Impact
Strategic Partnership
Serve as a trusted advisor to IT, Finance, and business leaders, building strong relationships and applying forward-looking technology risk judgment to anticipate change, identify emerging risks, and shape decisions.
Represent IT SOX within Adobe's broader assurance landscape, aligning with second-line and other assurance teams to reduce duplication and strengthen overall risk coverage.
IT SOX Program Ownership
Own the IT SOX compliance program from planning and scoping through testing, remediation, and reporting, setting the annual audit strategy alongside SOX PMO, Finance, IT control owners, our co-sourced provider, and external auditors.
Continually reshape the IT SOX roadmap and operating model, including capability and resourcing needs, to stay ahead of changes in Adobe's business and technology landscape rather than reacting to them.
Be the trusted counterpart for our external auditor on IT SOX matters, shaping scope, reliance, testing approach, and evidence expectations to raise efficiency without giving up assurance quality.
Own IT control deficiencies going beyond symptoms to root cause, weighing severity and financial risk, and validating that remediation actually holds up and prevents recurrence.
Systems, Controls & Technical Judgment
Understand Adobe's financial systems, data, and cloud architecture from infrastructure to finance applications to know which controls matter most.
Get ahead of major business and technology transformations by embedding risk and control thinking into the build rather than adding it retroactively.
Automation, Innovation & Training
Drive automation, analytics, and continuous monitoring to improve program effectiveness, and assess how AI and automation affect the control environment.
Train control owners and business partners on SOX responsibilities and control design, building control awareness across the organization over time.
People Leadership & Coaching
Coach and develop audit professionals through clear priorities, feedback, growth opportunities, and leadership development.
Build an inclusive, high-accountability culture focused on quality, collaboration, and continuous learning.
What you need to succeed
Experience
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Accounting, Information Systems, Computer Science, or a related field.
CPA, CISA, CIA, CISSP, or equivalent professional certification preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience related to IT SOX, IT audit, or technology risk, ideally including Big Four or large public company experience.
Hands-on experience with SAP environments, including SAP security, controls, and integration with SOX compliance programs. Experience with cloud technology and cloud control environments is strongly preferred.
Experience managing outsourced or co-sourced audit relationships and coordinating with external auditors.
People leadership experience in developing and growing a team.
Skills & Capabilities
Solid understanding of IT general and application controls (ITGC/ITAC), the COSO framework, and SOX 404 requirements.
Ability to reason about system architecture and data flows to make sound control scoping decisions across the technology stack.
Ability to apply data analytics and automation to audit and control design.
Strong root cause analysis and problem-solving skills, with a bias toward durable remediation over short-term fixes.
Exceptional written, verbal, and executive communication skills, able to translate complex technical and control topics into clear, actionable guidance.
High degree of integrity, sound judgment, and professional skepticism.

title: Principal Technical Product Manager, External Services, Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
description:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is looking for a Principal Product Manager – Technical to own and grow the Streaming Tables portfolio across the Kinesis and Amazon MSK product lines. Streaming Tables lands real-time streaming data directly into analytics-ready open table formats, such as Apache Iceberg on Amazon S3 and Amazon S3 Tables. It's a strategic bet that connects AWS streaming with the lakehouse.
As the senior product leader for this area, you'll set the multi-year vision and strategy, define the business, and build it into a major growth driver for AWS streaming. The goal is to make it zero-ETL to turn any stream on AWS into a fresh, governed table that's ready to query. That means aligning many teams on one direction: Kinesis, MSK, S3, Glue, Lake Formation, Athena, Redshift, and EMR.
You'll operate with a high degree of ambiguity and autonomy. You'll write the strategy narratives that AWS VPs and senior leaders use to make decisions, and you'll represent AWS to strategic customers, partners, and the open-source community. You'll also raise the bar for product management across the organization.
Key job responsibilities
- Own the vision, strategy, and 3+ year roadmap for Streaming Tables across Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon MSK. Define how the portfolio grows into new product lines and use cases.
- Own business outcomes for the portfolio: revenue, adoption, and active customers, plus investment cases and headcount asks in OP1/OP2 planning.
- Write PRFAQs, strategy 6-pagers, and leadership alignment documents, and drive decisions with VPs and senior leaders.
- Shape the technical direction with Principal Engineers on open table format delivery: Apache Iceberg (self-managed on S3 and S3 Tables), schema evolution, compaction, exactly-once semantics, freshness SLAs, and catalog integration.
- Drive alignment and shared roadmaps across AWS service teams so customers get one seamless experience from end to end.
- Represent AWS externally: strategic customers, partners, analysts, re:Invent and other conference talks, and engagement with the Apache Iceberg/Kafka communities.
- Define pricing, packaging, and go-to-market strategy with Product Marketing, Sales, and Solutions Architects.
- Set competitive strategy against Confluent Tableflow, Databricks, Snowflake, and others to keep AWS differentiated over the long term.
- Mentor PMs and raise the product management bar in the org, including serving as a bar raiser in hiring.
A day in the life
You might start your morning reviewing customer engagement data and refining your service roadmap based on emerging adoption patterns. By midday, you are in a working session with engineering leads, debating architectural trade-offs for a new capability and aligning on priorities. In the afternoon, you join a call with an enterprise customer to understand how they integrate your service into their technology stack, then translate those insights into a product narrative that will shape next quarter's investment decisions.
About the team

description:

You will be the day-to-day interface between Supply Chain, our manufacturing vendors and the NPD engineers who design our products. You make sure each group has the technical context, data and decisions it needs from the others. When a forecast changes, a supplier raises a constraint or a build stalls, you bring the right people together quickly, frame the trade-offs clearly and drive the issue to resolution.
We work quickly and practically. Rather than waiting for large software programs, you will use AI tools, agents, scripts and lightweight workflows to stand up working processes fast. You'll run them on a regular cadence with our partners and improve them as you learn. Once a process has proven itself, you will help turn it into durable tooling.
Key job responsibilities
- Drive the end-to-end program for interconnect products (optical modules, DAC/AEC, fiber and structured cabling) from forecast to delivery, and report progress and risks to NPD and Networking leadership through a regular business review.
- Act as the primary interface between Supply Chain, vendors and NPD engineering. Translate engineering constraints into supply implications and supply constraints into engineering decisions.
- Coordinate technical review of significant forecast changes (product mix or volume) with engineering and Supply Chain before they are shared with suppliers.
- Help keep long-range capacity commitments and short-range build signals distinct. Raise it early when an execution signal risks undoing a long-lead commitment (DSPs, lasers, PCBs, raw fiber materials, line capacity).
- Partner with engineering and Supply Chain to keep BOM and allocation data consistent, so sub-tier requirements line up across commodity managers.
- Run scenario analyses (for example a 50% demand increase or decrease) with Supply Chain and engineering to show where commitments break across components and sub-tiers, and help teams agree on the response.
- Work with vendors and Supply Chain to track supplier commitments and de-commitments for critical sub-tier parts
- Drive a weekly clear-to-build (CTB) review with vendors and Supply Chain that combines component availability against the build plan, escalates shortfalls early and handles excess inventory without stopping the line.
- Track capacity KPIs with our vendors. Work with engineering and site teams to validate capacity constraints when the data doesn't line up.
- Coordinate with Supply Chain and deployment teams on inventory at VMI hubs and rack integrators, so production plans reflect where finished units can actually go.
- Support rack integration improvements with engineering and integrators: rack portfolio standardization, production-readiness validation for new rack designs, first-pass yield, test time and the time from PO to start of assembly.
- Use AI tools and agents every day to automate data gathering, reconcile vendor and Supply Chain data, generate status reports and catch issues early.
- Build AI-assisted workflows that cut manual spreadsheet work for engineers and Supply Chain partners, and share what works across the team.
- Write requirements and work with software teams to turn proven processes and AI-assisted workflows into durable tools.
A day in the life
Your week might start with a CTB review across optics and fiber vendors, where an AI agent you set up has already reconciled the latest vendor data and flagged a laser shortfall weeks ahead. You then pull Supply Chain and engineering together to work through what a forecast revision means for supplier agreements. Later you follow up with a vendor on a capacity constraint that doesn't match their reported output, and join a call with a rack integrator on why a high-volume configuration keeps failing first-pass test. You write clear updates for leadership and turn this week's manual fixes into next week's automated workflow. Expect regular travel between Seattle and the Bay Area, as well as to supplier and integrator sites, mostly in Asia.

We work closely with the NPD switch and software teams, Global Supply Management, fabric and deployment teams, and our manufacturing partners worldwide. We value strong partnerships, mechanisms over good intentions, and a "trust, but verify" approach to the data we rely on.

title: AI Software Engineer - Calendar Intelligence
description:
Apple has changed how people live, connect, and work, and the Calendar team wants to rethink what a calendar can do for the people using it. A calendar knows when someone is busy. It knows very little about which of those commitments matter, which ones could move, or when would be a good time for something new. We're looking for an engineer to help answer those questions, on device and privately, for billions of people. The right person has strong machine learning foundations and is just as comfortable writing the software that ships a model as building the model itself. You'll help take ideas from a single sentence to a shipped feature, and you'll bring the evaluation that tells us whether it works.
In this role you'll drive the modeling and evaluation behind intelligence features in Calendar, from the first framing through launch, as part of a very collaborative team. A request will often start as one line, and you'll work with the team to turn it into a problem we can solve: what signal exists, what a good answer looks like, which approach fits, and how we'll know it's right. You'll design the evaluation before you build the model. That means the metrics, the eval sets, the baselines a model has to beat, and human review for the places where a metric can't tell you enough.
You won't always have good data, so part of the job is finding it and getting something useful out of it when there isn't much. You'll need to get real statistical strength out of priors, shared structure, and self-supervision. You'll also work with a range of large language models, on device and on server, deciding where a model call earns its cost, where a smaller model trained on a larger model's judgments does better, and where a well-tuned heuristic beats both.
You'll join a small team of senior systems engineers who ship this work across Apple's platforms, several of them with deep backgrounds in ML data engineering. There's no hard line between roles, so you'll write production code alongside them in whatever part of the stack the problem needs. Calendar also builds on signals and models from other ML teams across Apple, and a lot of this role is working with them: building on what they have, agreeing on shared interfaces, and recognizing when we need our own. You'll work closely with design and product as well. We need someone who writes clearly, can explain a model's tradeoffs to engineers who aren't ML specialists, and is comfortable driving a problem forward before the path is defined.
Minimum qualifications: Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, EE, Applied Mathematics, or related field with 2+ years experience in developing ML / AI driven software.
Proficiency in one or more of the following programming languages: Python, Swift, Objective-C, or C++
Experience developing software prototypes and features driven by Large Language Models and designing tool and function-calling interfaces, constructing context, and validating model output
Fluency with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, with good judgment about where to apply them and how to verify what they produce.
Experience driving an ambiguous problem with cross-functional partners, including other ML teams, from a loose idea through launch, and getting alignment on shared interfaces along the way.
Exceptional problem-solving skills, and the ability to drive alignment across teams on shared API surfaces
Preferred qualifications: Experience designing and developing systems that are efficient in resource constrained environments — latency, memory, and power budgets on device
Solid foundation in machine learning, probability, and statistics, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models in a framework such as PyTorch or JAX
A track record of designing the evaluation for what you ship: metrics, held-out sets, baselines, and noticing when a metric has stopped measuring what you care about
Proven ability to excel in a fast-paced development team

title: Fitness Sensing AI/ML Lead  - Sensing & Connectivity
description:

title: GNSS Hardware Systems Engineer
description:
Do you have a passion for invention and self-challenge? Do you thrive on pushing the limits of what’s considered feasible? Do you want to have an impact on every single Apple product?
Global Navigation Satellite Systems (GNSS) space vehicles transmit the power of a lightbulb, they are 13,000 miles away and are moving four kilometers per second. The received signals are commonly one hundred times weaker than cosmic microwave background radiation left over from the Big Bang and arrive next to interfering signals ten billion times stronger, just few MHz away.
Our GNSS team is part of Apple's Cellular team. We are a vertically coordinated engineering team spanning RF, mixed signal analog design, systems engineering, RTL design, design verification, firmware and software engineering, test, and validation. Our focus is on highly energy efficient and robust GNSS receiver design which continually outperform the previous iterations!
By collaborating with other product development groups across Apple, you’ll push the industry boundaries of what GNSS can do and improve the product experience for our customers across the world, something we are passionate about. We’d like you to consider being a part of our team!
In this technical role, you will define GNSS signal processing hardware architectures, developing system specification and modeling in MATLAB/C++/SystemC for RTL implementations. Your work will enable outstanding GNSS performance, balancing ultra-low power efficiency where possible with unparalleled performance and robustness when required.
Minimum qualifications: Minimum requirement of a bachelors degree.
Strong background in wireless communications space with focus on algorithmic development or digital hardware system design, e.g. GNSS, Connectivity, Cellular.
Familiarity with digital communication, signal processing, spread spectrum system, or systems theory.
Preferred qualifications: MSEE or beyond is preferred.
2+ years of proven experiences in GNSS baseband signal processing is preferred.
Proficiency with wireless communications system modeling and estimation theory.
Solid programming skills in MATLAB/C++/SystemC.
Good understanding of VLSI implementation, architecture and power optimization.
Healthy combination of innovation attitude and understanding of practical constraints of product development.
Excellent communication skills, both written & verbal especially in a multi-functional environment.

title: Hardware System Integration Electrical Engineer - Mac
description:

Experience in circuit design for a variety of domains including power, digital, analog, high-speed communications, programmable logic, and/or wireless. Preferred qualifications: Schematic capture and constraint-driven PCB layout using Cadence tools or similar.
Experience with PCB bringup and debug, including new or custom silicon, using standard EE lab equipment: Soldering, DMM, Oscilloscope, Logic Analyzer.
Experience with complex data analysis, data visualization and script development.

Excellent written and verbal communication and presentation skills.

description:

title: Software Development Engineer - System Analytics & Intelligence (SAIL)
description:
Core OS ships the foundational software that powers every Apple product. Accelerating developer productivity, elevating software quality, and shaping where the organization invests next all depend on turning massive amounts of workflow data into clear, strategic intelligence. The System Analytics & Intelligence (SAIL) team exists to do exactly that, identifying what matters most and driving meaningful improvements to the developer experience. Our goal is to help Core OS build better software faster.
We're looking for a software engineer who is excited to build the scalable services and data foundation that make this possible.

You'll engineer a unified platform that correlates events across many specialized systems to provide end-to-end observability of the Core OS development workflow.
We're looking for engineers who put the customer experience first, are passionate about building scalable and reliable services, and bring strong data engineering foundations. This role goes further than building and running services - you'll take part in every aspect of Core OS's software development lifecycle and own problems end to end, working cross-functionally with the engineering teams to use data to drive impact. title: Software Engineer, Applied ML
description:
Our mission is to personalize the Apple user experience based on where you go, when you’re there, and what those places mean to you. We’re developing intelligent systems that understand location context and help users achieve what they want, wherever they are. You’ve seen our work in action through suggested locations in Maps, Journaling Suggestions for outings and trips, and curated Memories in Photos. We’re seeking motivated, experienced engineers to elevate our software’s intelligence, performance, and impact. We are looking for a seasoned engineer who can help define where this work goes next, not just how it gets built. Do you have experience linking users and devices to points of interest on a map? Are you an ML practitioner energized by the challenge of delivering rich contextual intelligence within a tight resource budget? If so, we’d love to hear from you.
As a seasoned engineer on the location technologies team, you will drive the direction for feature development and strategy. As part of this role, you'll join a team of software engineers and researchers focused on identifying behavioral patterns and you will help shape new and enhanced user experiences by collaborating closely with teams across sensing, Siri, and apps. You will partner with engineering, product, and research leadership to set a multi-year technical roadmap, translate ambiguous product goals into clear technical strategy, and make the architectural and investment trade-offs that follow.
Excited to take ownership of complex, end-to-end problems? You’ll design, build, and evaluate production ML systems that infer a device’s patterns by inference on data like GPS, Wi-Fi, and accelerometers and higher semantic signals, combining estimation techniques with machine learning. You’ll test and refine your work, use it yourself, track metrics, and iterate for quality. You will help identifing new opportunities for location intelligence across Apple’s products, and mentor engineers to raise the technical bar for the whole team.
Minimum qualifications: Experience building and shipping production software, including technical leadership of multi-engineer projects.
Experience shipping production software for mobile and/or other resource-constrained devices. Tight memory, CPU, and schedule constraints motivate you and ignite your creativity. Capability of creating, analyzing, and modifying SW functionality, ideally in C++/Obj-C/Swift codebases.
Data processing: Skilled in working with large, noisy datasets.
Experience with libraries like NumPy, pandas, scikit-learn, and PyTorch or TensorFlow.
Hands-on experience with applied probability, statistics, and empirical and/or ML algorithms. Classical estimation, signal processing, and/or training supervised ML models are relevant.
Bachelor’s or graduate degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field.
Preferred qualifications: Proven track record of setting technical strategy and roadmaps for ML-driven product features, and of influencing decisions across organizations without direct authority.
Machine Learning algorithms: Strong grasp of supervised/unsupervised learning, regression, classification, clustering, and model evaluation techniques.
Having worked as an ML practitioner in an industrial setting.
Experience mentoring and growing engineers, and building alignment among technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Laser focus on customer impact and product experience.
Some professional background in location and/or other wireless sensing technologies, including for example, GPS/GNSS, WiFi, indoor localization, and/or discrete localization.
Excellent communication, verbally and in writing. You can present strategy and technical trade-offs clearly to senior leadership. You can succeed in a collaborative environment, and are comfortable with what will sometimes feel like a high degree of uncertainty.
You can innovate within tight memory, CPU, and schedule constraints, and deliver on time. These constraints motivate you and ignite your creativity.

The Emerging Markets team promotes growth in local economies by building meaningful partnerships with merchants across underdeveloped, high-opportunity markets. Expand DoorDash’s presence by traveling to emerging markets and developing new restaurant partnerships.

title: Senior Manager, New Verticals - Fulfillment Dasher Strategy & Operations
location: New York, NY; San Francisco, CA; Seattle, WA; Los Angeles, CA; Seattle, WA; Washington, DC; Chicago, IL; Tempe, AZ
description:
About the Team
New Verticals is an exciting team at DoorDash that is building and scaling new ways to delight our customers beyond restaurant delivery. New Verticals owns delivery businesses across Grocery, Convenience, Alcohol, Retail, Pharmacy and DashMart. Our Fulfillment Strategy & Operations team has three mandates: onboard merchants well, fulfill every order with speed and accuracy, and keep improving our logistics network. We do it by finding efficiencies, shipping product tooling and launching operational processes at scale.
About the Role
We are scaling our New Verticals Fulfillment Strategy & Operations team. Strategy & Operations combines strategic thinking, strong analytical problem solving, and operational execution to identify opportunities, develop solutions, and drive measurable business impact for our New Verticals businesses while working cross-functionally across Product, Engineering, Data Science, Machine Learning, and Operations to bring these solutions to life.
We’re looking for a Senior Manager to lead a team of three focused on two critical areas of New Verticals fulfillment - merchant experience and occasion quality .
For merchants who pick and pack their own DoorDash orders, you’ll set the strategy for improving the tools and workflows they use every day. You’ll work with Product and Engineering to build features that help merchants fulfill orders accurately and efficiently, while unlocking growth for their businesses.
You’ll also lead our approach to fulfillment quality during occasions—our highest-volume days, when getting the customer experience right is especially important. You’ll identify risks, develop plans with cross-functional partners and help ensure orders are delivered with high quality at scale.
This role combines strategy, analytics, product development and hands-on operations. You’ll partner with teams across regions, including Product Managers in EMEA, to identify shared opportunities and build solutions that work for local markets.
You’re excited about this opportunity because you will…
Lead : You'll spearhead cross-functional projects, collaborating with Engineers, Data Scientists, and Product Managers to develop and implement tech solutions that increase selection across our New Vertical offerings.
Strategize: You will own and deliver on improving key quality and cost metrics. You’ll create and execute quarterly and annual strategic plans aligned with product capabilities to elevate order quality.
Build : You will build strategic initiatives and drive innovation across our offerings; this can vary from AI-powered predictions to improving the overall shopping experience. This means everything from high-level strategy to operational details.
Analyze. You love working with data to drive business decision-making and are familiar with SQL.
We’re excited about you because…
You are an operator. You don’t hesitate to get in the weeds and operate at the lowest level of detail, but you’re also able to think long-term. You are excited to experience our operation firsthand to inform your strategy.
You solve problems from first principles. You’re excited to think innovatively, and you resist “this is how it’s always been done” thinking.
You’re analytical. You possess a sharp analytical mind, and can extract and communicate meaningful insights from data to drive strategic decisions. You are comfortable with SQL and data visualization tools.
You’re AI native. You root cause problems with a systems first approach and can identify how to automate repeatable tasks using AI tools like Claude, Cursor, Gemini or Copilot.
You have 8-12+ years of experience. You’ve succeeded in high-performing cultures (tech, operations, strategy, consulting, banking, startups or a related experience). Prior experience in e-commerce fulfillment or marketplace operations is a plus!
You have prior people management experience. You have hired & developed a team.
You have a completed Bachelor’s Degree ideally in finance, economics, computer science, engineering, or a related field . An MBA is highly preferred!

title: Senior Strategic Account Marketing Lead
description:
About MISUMI Americas
MISUMI Americas, a division of MISUMI Group, is a leading provider of standard, configurable, and custom manufacturing solutions. By integrating a vast catalog of components with a world-class digital manufacturing platform, MISUMI Americas empowers engineers and procurement teams to accelerate innovation across the entire product lifecycle. With operations in the San Francisco Bay Area and Chicago, the company serves as a vital partner for the most innovative companies in the Americas.
Impact In This Role
As the Senior Strategic Account Marketing Lead at MISUMI Americas, you will work side by side with the sales reps who own your assigned accounts. You will take their account plans, what customers are telling us, and our revenue goals, and turn them into practical, creative marketing campaigns. These campaigns should spark engagement, create and move deals forward, and strengthen customer relationships.
This is not a role for a single-channel specialist. You will build and lead growth plans for each account, using both hands-on and large-scale tactics. These include customer visits, lunch-and-learns, direct mail and swag, executive outreach, events, targeted email and nurture programs, paid ads, sales support materials, and account-specific content. You do not have to create every asset or run every channel yourself. You do need to pick the right mix, bring in the right partners, and see the work through to results you can measure.
What You’ll Be Doing
Become a trusted, proactive marketing partner to the Account Executives and sales leaders for a named portfolio of Strategic and Key Accounts. Maintain a regular operating cadence with each seller to understand account priorities, opportunities, whitespace, risks, and next steps.
Translate account plans, account research, buyer and buying-group insights, intent signals, opportunity data, and customer engagement into focused account-growth strategies and quarterly activation plans.
Own the end-to-end planning, orchestration, and execution of 1:1, 1:few, and 1:many account marketing programs. Select the right mix of high-touch and scalable tactics based on the account objective, buying stage, audience, and expected impact.
Develop creative, practical account plays that help Sales earn attention and create momentum. Examples include customer-office visits, lunch-and-learns, executive meetings, local customer experiences, direct mail and swag, targeted events, customer workshops, outbound support, account-specific content, and digital nurture programs.
Partner with Lifecycle, Performance Marketing, Field and Events, Content, Product Marketing, Design, Sales Development, and external vendors to activate cohesive campaigns. Write clear briefs, establish ownership and timelines, resolve blockers, and ensure every program is delivered to a high bar.
Work with Web, Lifecycle and Performance Marketing to create and optimize targeted email, nurture, retargeting, paid media, landing-page, and audience programs for assigned accounts when those tactics will advance the account objective.
Drive customers and prospects to MISUMI Americas events and create thoughtful pre-event, onsite, and post-event account plans that convert event participation into meaningful sales follow-up and pipeline progress.
Work with Content and PMMs to build the sales enablement required for each activation, including messaging, outreach guidance, follow-up plans, templates, snippets, talking points, and clear seller actions. Ensure Sales understands the plan and follows through.
Manage assigned program budgets and vendors with an ROI mindset. Test, learn, reallocate investment, and know when to stop, revise, or scale an account play.
Use Salesforce, Marketo, Reachdesk, Sigma, intent data, account engagement data, and other available signals to identify opportunity, prioritize investment, and measure impact. Maintain a clear view of account engagement, buying-group reach, opportunity creation and progression, pipeline, conversion, velocity, win rate, and revenue influence.
Share account-level learnings, results, and recommendations with Sales and Marketing. Turn successful plays into repeatable programs and quickly address underperforming tactics.
Execute directly when speed and quality require it. This role is expected to be a hands-on operator, not solely a strategist, coordinator, or requester of work from other teams.
Travel to customer offices, MISUMI Americas events, industry events, and internal meetings when in-person engagement can accelerate an account objective.
How We’ll Measure Success
Success in this role is measured by business impact and sales-partner effectiveness, not campaign activity alone. In the first year, this person will:
Establish productive working relationships and a clear account-growth cadence with the sellers for their assigned Strategic and Key Accounts.
Deliver account plans and integrated activations that are directly tied to seller priorities, customer needs, and pipeline goals.
Increase meaningful engagement with priority contacts and buying groups, create or advance qualified opportunities, and contribute to pipeline progression, opportunity velocity, win rate, and revenue across the supported portfolio.
Build repeatable, data-informed account plays that combine high-touch experiences with scalable lifecycle and performance tactics.
Earn a reputation with Sales and Marketing for creativity, responsiveness, sound judgment, operational follow-through, and measurable impact.
What Makes This Role Different
This role sits at the intersection of account strategy, field execution, digital activation, and sales partnership. It is not limited to digital marketing, paid media, event production, project management, or account research. Candidates must bring broad marketing judgment and be comfortable moving between customer-facing experiences, account-specific campaigns, and scaled programs.
The role owns the account marketing strategy, activation plan, cross-functional orchestration, seller adoption, and performance readout for the assigned portfolio. Channel and functional teams provide their specialized expertise; this role brings those capabilities together into the right account solution and owns the outcome.
Desired Traits
8+ years of B2B marketing experience in account-based marketing, strategic account marketing, field marketing, demand generation, or a closely related revenue-marketing role.
Demonstrated experience partnering directly with enterprise, strategic, or key-account sellers to build and execute account plans that contributed to pipeline, opportunity progression, and revenue.
Proven ability to develop and execute integrated campaigns across both high-touch and digital channels, including customer events or experiences, direct mail or gifting, sales outreach support, email or nurture, paid or performance programs, and content.
Track record of taking programs from insight and strategy through detailed execution, optimization, and performance reporting.
Strong commercial judgment and comfort prioritizing a portfolio of accounts against revenue opportunity, sales priorities, and expected return on investment.
Customer-facing confidence and experience representing Marketing in seller and customer conversations, including onsite engagements when appropriate.
Excellent cross-functional project leadership. Able to write clear briefs, align stakeholders, build realistic workback plans, resolve ambiguity, and keep multiple time-sensitive programs moving.
Analytical fluency and experience using CRM, marketing automation, account engagement, and intent data to make decisions and measure results. Salesforce and Marketo experience strongly preferred.
Strong written, verbal, and presentation communication skills.
Comfort in a fast-moving environment where the right play is not always obvious and initiative matters.
Ability to travel up to 25% within the U.S. for customer-office visits, MISUMI | Fictiv events, industry events, and internal meetings.
Preferred Traits
Experience marketing to complex B2B buying groups in a technical, industrial, manufacturing, or supply-chain environment.
Experience with ABM platforms, intent-data tools, audience development, and account-level reporting.
Experience producing or supporting executive programs, customer workshops, lunch-and-learns, field events, and direct-mail or gifting programs.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.
Physical Traits
The physical demands described here are representative of those an employee must meet to successfully perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
While performing the duties of this role, the employee routinely is required to sit, walk, talk, hear, use hands to keyboard and handle objects, and occasionally stoop, kneel, crouch, twist, crawl, reach, and stretch.
Ability to travel up to 25% within the U.S. for customer-office visits, MISUMI Americas events, industry events, and internal meetings in Oakland, CA and Schaumburg, IL.
Perks and Benefits
Competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance
401K plan
Parental leave programs
Paid volunteer days
And much, much more!
Salary Range: $130,000 to $160,000 per year, based upon experience
Interested in learning more?  We look forward to hearing from you soon.
We’re actively seeking teammates who:
Bring diverse perspectives and experience to our culture and company.
Excel at being part of a strong, empathetic team.
Thrive in an environment emphasizing respect, honesty, collaboration, and growth.
Have an ‘always learning’ mindset that celebrates learning, not just wins.
Help us continue to build a world-class organization that values the contributions of all of our teammates
We encourage applications from members of underrepresented groups, including but not limited to women, members of the LGBTQ community, people of color, people with disabilities, and veterans.

description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Staff Validation Engineer, Electrical Systems to join our Electrical & Software Test organization. In this role you will be the technical lead for system-level testing of electrical, software, and control systems on test assets that deliver learnings on our Power Conversion Systems (DC/DC, inverter, etc.) and Network Systems (plant-level communications, etc.). These assets are a cornerstone of our validation strategy.



You will be deeply accountable for identifying, planning, and executing system-level tests that deliver learnings to our Power Conversion Systems and Network Systems teams, and for turning those learnings into design changes, requirements, and product-readiness decisions. The ideal candidate pairs rigorous technical depth and first-principles thinking with the leadership required to align cross-functional teams and mentor growing engineers and technicians.



This is an exciting opportunity to contribute to the scaling of our battery technology and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Identify the system-level tests, test assets, and operating conditions needed to retire the highest-risk electrical, software, and control system unknowns.

 - Architect comprehensive test plans and procedures that validate Power Conversion Systems (DC/DC, inverter) and Network Systems (plant-level communications) behaviors across electrical, software, and control layers.

 - Act as the primary technical bridge between design teams (electrical hardware, software, controls), test engineering, and product management to translate high-level requirements into executable validation strategies.

 - Partner closely with Site Operations and Facilities teams to manage the infrastructure footprint, power requirements, safety protocols (hazard reviews, FMEA), and continuous uptime of test assets.

 - Lead the day-to-day execution of test campaigns. When anomalies occur, spearhead root-cause analysis (RCA) and triage across electrical hardware, software, controls, and test infrastructure.

 - Synthesize complex test data into clear, actionable engineering reports and leadership dashboards to gate product milestones.

 - Act as a force multiplier by coaching, mentoring, and leveling up junior engineers and test technicians.

 - Champion a culture of safety, cleanliness, 5S, and rigorous documentation within the testing lab environment.




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - 8+ years of experience in systems validation, integration testing, or hardware test engineering (ideally within power electronics, grid storage, renewables, electric vehicles, or aerospace).

 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems, Controls, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

 - Deep familiarity with power conversion hardware (DC/DC converters, inverters, rectifiers), high-voltage power distribution, protection, and control architectures.

 - Experience with high-power industrial systems, grid-tied equipment, or power electronics at utility or industrial scale.

 - Proficiency with test automation frameworks (e.g., Python, LabVIEW, MATLAB/Simulink) and data analysis pipelines for high-rate electrical data.

 - Familiarity with network protocols standard to industrial, grid, and automotive systems (CAN, Modbus, Ethernet, EtherCAT, DNP3, IEC 61850).

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, evolving hardware startup environment; able to carve out a path forward when requirements are fluid.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work cross-functionally and present test findings to design, controls, and leadership audiences in a fast-paced environment.

description:
Job Description:
Miller Electric is building an internal creative team capable of producing world-class work for one of the most respected brands in welding. That means moving beyond reactive task execution and becoming a trusted creative partner to the business.
The Graphic Designer creates thoughtful, distinctive, and highly accurate work across print, digital, environmental, and campaign applications. This person must care equally about the strength of the idea and the quality of the execution. Good work is not finished until it communicates clearly, supports the business objective, reflects the Miller brand, and is technically ready for its intended use.
We are looking for a designer who is curious, accountable, receptive to feedback, and motivated to continually improve. This person should bring energy and passion to the work while remaining dependable, mature, and composed when timelines tighten or priorities change. This is an onsite position located in Appleton, WI.
How We Work
Our goal is not simply to make things look good or complete a list of requests. We expect every member of the creative team to:
Understand the purpose, audience, and business objective before beginning the work.
Ask why, challenge assumptions respectfully, and bring a recommendation—not only a question.
Take ownership of the outcome from initial concept through final delivery.
Communicate the true status of work and raise risks, missing information, or deadline concerns early.
Treat feedback as part of the creative process and separate personal ego from critique of the work.
Maintain professional composure and a solution-focused attitude when projects become difficult.
Care about typography, hierarchy, imagery, spacing, consistency, production details, and every element that affects quality.
Respect brand, legal, compliance, and production requirements while still pursuing original creative solutions.
Share information, help teammates, and contribute to a positive, accountable team environment.
Stay curious about our products, customers, markets, competitors, culture, and the broader creative industry.
Bring passion and enjoyment to the work without sacrificing focus or discipline.
Key Responsibilities
Develop creative concepts and finished designs for campaigns, product launches, catalogs, brochures, sales materials, trade shows, environmental graphics, packaging, presentations, digital content, and other brand applications.
Translate creative briefs, business objectives, audience needs, and brand strategy into effective visual communication.
Develop work that feels specific to Miller, its customers, and its markets rather than relying on generic design solutions.
Apply established brand standards consistently while using sound judgment to determine when a project requires a new or adapted solution.
Present design recommendations clearly and explain the reasoning behind creative decisions.
Prepare accurate, production-ready files for print and digital use, including dimensions, bleeds, safe areas, links, resolution, color modes, typography, and output settings.
Review and preflight every deliverable before release to identify errors, inconsistencies, and production risks.
Manage multiple projects, maintain accurate status, and communicate changing priorities or concerns early.
Incorporate feedback constructively and demonstrate that lessons from one project have been applied to the next.
Collaborate with marketing partners, business divisions, printers, vendors, agencies, and other creative team members throughout development and production.
Maintain organized working files, packaged final files, and clear handoff documentation.
Help improve templates, workflows, asset libraries, and production processes.
Develop a working knowledge of Miller products, customers, markets, channels, and the welding industry.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in graphic design, visual communication, or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
Three or more years of professional graphic design experience preferred.
A portfolio demonstrating strong typography, composition, visual hierarchy, brand application, and production execution.
Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud, particularly InDesign, Illustrator, and Photoshop.
Strong understanding of print production, file preparation, color management, image resolution, bleeds, and vendor handoffs.
Ability to manage multiple assignments, establish priorities, and meet deadlines in a fast-moving environment.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering accurate finished work.
Ability to receive direct feedback professionally and use it to improve the work.
Clear written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work independently while contributing positively to a team.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting an established consumer, industrial, manufacturing, or business-to-business brand.
Experience with catalogs, trade-show graphics, packaging, environmental graphics, or other complex print applications.
Experience working with outside printers, production vendors, agencies, photographers, or illustrators.
Familiarity with digital design, presentation design, asset-management systems, and project-management platforms.
Genuine interest in products, customers, and the environments in which the brand is used.
What Success Looks Like
Work is consistently thoughtful, distinctive, brand-appropriate, and production-ready.
Projects move forward with clear status, realistic commitments, and early escalation of risks.
Design decisions reflect the audience, business objective, channel, and Miller brand.
Deliverables require less corrective review because details are addressed before release.
Feedback produces visible improvement across future projects.
Files and handoffs are organized so teammates and vendors can use them without avoidable rework.
The designer develops a strong creative point of view while remaining collaborative and open to direction.
The designer strengthens the team through reliability, curiosity, accountability, and a genuine commitment to excellent work.

Primary Function of the Position
The Manager Mechanical Design Engineering leads cross-functional teams to maintain and improve the design, production, and service of the da Vinci® Surgical Systems.  This includes determining root cause of complex problems with electro-mechanical components, manufacturing process and system performance. This also includes identifying mechanical design and manufacturing process solutions to improve performance, cost, and reliability, and perform the development, documentation, verification, and implementation of these solutions. The successful candidate must be a “player / coach” fcomfortable with some individual technical contribution as well as the leadership of deeply technical individual contributors.
Essential Job Duties
Leads cross-functional project teams to design, develop and verify modifications to robotic or other complex mechanisms.
Investigate and determine root cause of latent and emerging design, manufacturing or material defects
Develop, design, test, document, and implement solutions for these defects according to corporate standards and departmental operating procedures
Identify, develop, and implement alternate part fabrication methods and sources to reduce hardware cost and/or improve strength of supply chain
Develop and execute design verification/validation test protocols and document results in test reports
Support product risk assessments, Corrective and Preventive Actions, and quality/regulatory audits as required
Interface with teams across Intuitive including mechanical, software, systems analysis, manufacturing, test, supply chain, quality, regulatory, service, tech pubs, etc.
Provide administrative leadership and control for planning, staffing, budgeting, and project/program cost tracking.
Establish project teams, assign tasks, set priorities, establish metrics, and track progress against overall goals.
Recognize and attract top talent, mentor, and train team members through one-on-one coaching as well as team wide initiatives.
Support quality assurance, product reliability, and product regulatory initiatives in responding to customer concerns and other product requirements.
Required Skills and Experience
Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, analysis, debug, verification, transfer to manufacturing, and sustainment.
Understand concepts of FMEAs, design input/output, and requirement traceability
Technical proficiency in mechanism design and robotics
Design, manufacture and troubleshooting of electromechanical components and assemblies including brushless DC motors, brakes, encoders and other sensors
Design, manufacture and troubleshooting of precision mechanical components including bearings, gears, ball screws and linear actuators
Component selection and design for reliability and manufacturability
Proficiency at failure analysis
Mechanical analysis, including statics, dynamics, kinematics, stress, fatigue, thermal, and reliability
Follow good documentation principles and configuration control methods
Demonstrated knowledge of a wide variety of manufacturing processes
Metallurgical heat treatment, stress relief, grinding/lapping
Component fabrication methods including CNC machining, wire EDM, brazing, and surface coatings
High-volume fabrication methods including plastic injection molding, metal-injection molding, stamping, aluminum/steel casting (sand, investment, die)
Comfortable operating machine shop, measurement, and test equipment
Proven ability to lead departmental and cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives from concept through completion
Proven ability to prioritize and organize while guiding your team to tackle many complex projects simultaneously
Ability to communicate effectively (written, oral) across all levels and organizations
Ability to rigorously adhere to and create robust processes
Ability to utilize deep technical knowledge and broad expertise to achieve company objectives in creative and effective ways
Real excitement to learn and get to the bottom of tough technical problems
Passion for creating robust, reliable products with a strong commitment to high product quality
Excel in a fast paced, high transaction, mass-production environment
Sense of shared responsibility and reward
Required Education and Training
Minimum Bachelor’s Degree in Mechanical Engineering or similar technical field
Minimum 8 years of experience designing and manufacturing electromechanical products
1-3 year as a people manager or prior management responsibilities through project management or team leadership efforts
Fluency in ASME Y14.5 GD&T and tolerance stack analysis
Design, analyze and document components, structures, and mechanical assemblies in SolidWorks or similar CAD software
Preferred Skills and Experience
Advanced degree in Mechanical Engineering or similar technical field
Experience in medical device industry and/or experience in a regulated industry
Experience with Statistical Process Control in a Mass Production environment
Mechatronics experience.
Capability to use MATLAB to create or modify test scripts and system software

description:

If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
The Embedded Platform Software team designs and builds the foundational software infrastructure for next-generation surgical robotic systems. We are looking for a high-energy, talented Staff Embedded Software Engineer to join the Embedded Networking Software team, within the Multiport Platform Software group. If you’ve built in-vehicle networks, automotive middleware, or real-time robot communication stacks, your experience translates directly to what we do.
We are a small group that works in a focused, high-energy environment working on New Product Development. We believe in applying first principles thinking, data driven decision making, continuous learning, and systematic planning to deliver results and achieve our goals.
Are you passionate about technology?
Do you want to have a direct impact on helping people live better lives?
Are you interested in the medical applications of robotics?
Do you like building deterministic, distributed systems, like zonal vehicle networks or multi-node robot control stacks?
Does working in a multidisciplinary, systems-oriented design team sound exciting?
Your Role
You will be a technical leader on the team developing our flagship product, dV5. The team's focus is to enhance and extend the dV5 robotic embedded network across Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) layers 1–5, with a focus on PHYs, MACs, Ethernet switches, and the drivers that tie them together, and apply that deep understanding to new surgical robotic systems. The challenges will feel familiar to anyone who has built vehicle or robot networks: mixed-criticality traffic, precise time synchronization, and safety-critical determinism. You will own the architecture, set the multi-year technical direction, and grow the engineers around you.
Your Responsibilities
In your first year in this role, you will:
Design, develop, and deliver features architectures across the embedded network stack and help define the technical roadmap across:
Reliability, including redundancy and fault tolerance strategies
Performance architecture for growing data transfer needs: low latency switching, traffic shaping, queue management
Own the architecture and development of Ethernet MAC, PHY, and switch drivers (Linux and RTOS), including bring-up on new silicon and boards
Define and implement automotive Ethernet switch configuration: VLANs, QoS/priority mapping, ACLs/filtering, port mirroring, and static/dynamic forwarding tables
Implement and tune TSN features in switch hardware and drivers for safety-critical deterministic traffic
Set the technical direction and standards for Layer 2/Layer 3 software, Ethernet MAC and PHY drivers, and deterministic real-time paths for safety critical data, applying queueing theory
Lead design and code reviews, mentor senior and mid-level engineers, and raise the bar on design quality and debugging rigor while staying hands-on in the highest-risk code
Serve as the technical authority on hardware integration, and lead escalations on the hardest hardware-software networking failures (JTAG, GDB, protocol analyzers)
Drive alignment across cross functional teams such as FPGA, Electrical (board bring-up and signal integrity), Application Development, Algorithms, Clinical, and Manufacturing to negotiate requirements and resolve architectural tradeoffs
Influence build-versus-buy and Ethernet switch/PHY silicon selection, working directly with vendors, and make the case for investments that retire technical debt
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree with 10+ years, or Master’s degree with 8+ years, of industry experience in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related discipline
Demonstrated technical leadership on complex systems: owning architecture, mentoring engineers, and influencing direction across organizational boundaries
A natural communicator with strong critical thinking, and clarity of thought who can explain architectural tradeoffs to engineers and executives alike
Expert networking fundamentals across the OSI stack, with deep expertise in L2/L3 (Ethernet switching, IP) and working knowledge of L1 (PHY), a solid understanding of TCP/IP stack internals and Ethernet switching fabric design, and expert C/C++ skills for embedded development
Deep experience architecting and delivering high-speed networking software in automotive, robotics, or industrial, including low-level Ethernet MAC/PHY driver development
Experience with Linux and embedded RTOS environments (e.g., FreeRTOS, ThreadX, Zephyr, QNX, VxWorks), with a strong understanding of memory management, concurrency, and interrupt handling
Demonstrated experience leveraging new tools and technology, such as AI coding assistants, to increase speed, and driving adoption across a team
Preferred Experience
Experience defining multi-generation technical strategy or platform roadmaps for a shipping hardware product
Strong hardware-software fluency: schematics, datasheets, reasoning across system abstractions
Hands-on experience configuring and writing drivers for managed Ethernet switch silicon (e.g., NXP SJA11xx, Marvell, Microchip, Broadcom), including register-level programming over SPI/MDIO/SMI
Hands-on experience with IEEE 802.1 TSN/AVB (802.1AS/gPTP, Qbv, Qav, Qci, CB/FRER), high-availability redundancy on real hardware, L2 switching (VLANs, QoS, segmentation), and Automotive Ethernet (100/1000BASE-T1, BASE-T1S), including zonal or domain controller architectures
Familiarity with communication middleware (DDS, SOME/IP, ROS 2) and how it maps onto L2 QoS/TSN configuration
Experience with real-time industrial or robotics networks such as EtherCAT, PROFINET IRT, or EtherNet/IP
Exposure to functional safety standards (such as IEC 62304, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, IEC 60601, ISO 26262) and embedded network security such as MACsec and IPsec

description:

Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the da Vinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Qualifications:
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

description:

The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.

Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
