Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.

Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.

Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

description:
Invenergy is North America’s largest privately held developer, owner, and operator of power infrastructure. With 25 years of trusted execution, we deliver reliable, affordable energy through a diverse portfolio that includes natural gas, solar, land-based wind, energy storage, transmission, and domestic manufacturing. Job Description
Position Overview
As an Assistant General Counsel, Commercial Transactions you will be focused on energy and infrastructure project development and specific commercial transactions related thereto.
You will provide professional legal advice, counsel, and guidance to support the development, construction, finance and management of Invenergy’s growing renewable and clean energy portfolio.
Responsibilities
Provide legal support to Invenergy’s project development, commercial execution and finance and capital markets teams on a wide variety of commercial transactions, including power purchase and similar offtake agreements, build-transfer agreements, commodity and currency hedge and trading agreements, interconnection agreements, EPC agreements, equipment supply agreements, operations and maintenance agreements as well as acquisitions and dispositions, debt financing, cash and tax equity financings, and joint venture agreements.
Provide guidance on transaction structuring.
Support the drafting and negotiation of project and financing documentation.
Select and efficiently manage sophisticated outside counsel.
Ensure consistency across transactions and compliance with internal policies.
The position will also provide legal advice and support in other areas of the company as needed and able.
The position will require overtime and travel at times.
Minimum Qualifications
JD degree and admission to practice law in at least one U.S. state
5-7+ years of experience either within a law firm or as in-house counsel supporting utility scale energy project development, finance and M&A transactions.
Experience drafting, negotiating, and advising on sophisticated energy related project development, finance and M&A documentation
Proven ability as a legal lead to drive transactions to successful completion.
Experience researching and analyzing applicable laws and regulations; conducting due diligence reviews; and managing transaction closings.
Able to work cross-functionally with internal and external stakeholders under minimal supervision.
Excellent communication skills and ability to relay complex concepts to members of management
Able to work under minimal supervision
Base Pay
$180,000.00 - $216,000.00 USD Annual
Bonus: 25% - 40%

description:

Job Description
Position Overview
The Associate, AI Adoption & Learning will design, execute, and evaluate assigned learning programs that build AI fluency and drive adoption of Microsoft Copilot and other approved AI tools across Invenergy.
Reporting to Organizational Effectiveness, the person in this role will collaborate with Talent Development, Enterprise Analytics & AI, technology teams, and business stakeholders to translate complex business needs into practical learning experiences. This on-site position is located at Invenergy’s downtown Chicago, IL office.

Develop and deliver practical, role-based learning pathways that build employee AI skills and drive adoption, quickly identifying employees’ starting skills and barriers to tailor training and inform the broader AI learning plan.
Apply instructional design and adult learning principles to turn complex workflows and AI use cases into instructor-led training, eLearning, microlearning, demonstrations, and job aids.
Facilitate in-person and virtual training, workshops, and office hours that help employees use Microsoft Copilot and other approved AI tools effectively.
Build AI fluency through practical instruction in prompting, evaluating AI outputs, understanding tool limitations, and applying responsible AI practices in alignment with company guidance.
Partner with subject matter experts and technology teams to translate tool capabilities and employee use cases into clear, repeatable learning materials.
Support program facilitators through training resources, train-the-trainer sessions, and communities of practice that reinforce learning and adoption.
Keep learning content and guidance current as AI tools, features, access requirements, and company policies change; validate updates with the appropriate teams.
Manage assigned AI enablement programs, including timelines, stakeholder coordination, communications, learning platform content, and follow-up; resolve delivery issues and escalate risks or decisions beyond the role’s scope.

Bachelor’s degree in Business, Education, Communications, Human Resources, Organizational Development, or a related field.
Minimum of 4 years of experience in learning and development, technical or professional training, enablement, or program management with a substantial training component; or a relevant advanced degree and a minimum of 2 years of directly relevant experience.
Excellent written, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills, with the ability to teach audiences with widely varying levels of knowledge.
Hands-on experience using Microsoft Copilot or comparable generative AI tools in workplace scenarios, including evaluating outputs and following responsible AI practices.
Strong collaboration, program management, and prioritization skills, with the ability to influence stakeholders and independently manage assigned initiatives in a complex, matrixed organization.
Demonstrated experience owning learning programs or workstreams from needs analysis through content design, facilitation, and evaluation, including adapting delivery to complex business needs.
Eligible to work in the United States without the need for employer visa sponsorship now or in the future.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building curriculum and role-based learning pathways for a large, distributed audience, particularly in a technical, engineering, or energy environment.
Experience driving adoption of an internal platform or technology in partnership with the team responsible for the tool.
Experience building AI fluency programs and AI training facilitator networks to deliver training.
Experience using instructional design and evaluation frameworks, such as ADDIE or Kirkpatrick, to measure learning beyond completion rates.
Familiarity with Viva Learning, Docebo, or comparable learning platforms and digital content development tools.
Training professional certification, such as Associate Professional in Talent Development (APTD), Certified Professional in Talent Development (CPTD), or Certified Professional in Training Management (CPTM).

description:

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with ownership of problem definition, process design, integrated planning, and end-to-end delivery.

You will work across Compute Finance, Infrastructure Accounting, Capacity Planning, Fleet, Design & Construction, Operations, Procurement, Legal, Data, and Engineering.  - Drive consistent tracking of contracts, tranches, delivery events, and capacity acceptance. Connect committed spend to provisioned, accepted, allocated, and used capacity to support forecasting and financial review.

 - Coordinate reliable ingestion and normalization of cloud service provider usage, billing, invoice, and delivery data. Establish data owners, completeness checks, and traceability to financial outputs.

 - Improve compute billing, accrual, and allocation processes through consistent pricing rules, SKU mappings, telemetry and organizational tags, reconciliations, and controlled handling of manual adjustments.

 - Partner with application, AI, and data engineers to translate requirements into integrations and automation across contract, procurement, compute data, and finance platforms, with monitoring and governed change controls.

 - Align Infrastructure, Finance, Accounting, Procurement, Legal, and Engineering on decisions and dependencies. Manage scope, risks, vendor dependencies, and change requests; escalate with clear options and business impact.

 - Lead end-to-end testing, UAT, rollout, training, and handoff to operational owners. Define success measures for traceability, data quality, manual effort, exception resolution, close readiness, and adoption.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - 8+ years of experience in project or program management, finance transformation, infrastructure operations, or enterprise systems delivery in complex, scaled environments.

title: Subject Matter Expert, Legal
description:
About the Team

We are building AI systems that help people tackle complex, consequential work in the legal industry. Law demands careful reasoning, precise language, and sound judgment: understanding the facts, identifying the right questions, weighing competing interpretations, and helping clients decide what to do next. We see an opportunity for AI to help legal professionals work with greater rigor and focus more of their time on the problems that matter most.

Our team works across Research, Product, Engineering, and Go-to-Market to build AI capabilities and products for legal work. Our customers include the top law firms in the world as well as in-house legal departments of some of the largest businesses in the world. We translate the realities of practice into evaluations, training signals, and useful tools, with the ambition of making AI a trusted part of how lawyers research, analyze, draft, and advise.



About the Role

We are looking for a Subject Matter Expert in Law who brings the judgment and practical experience developed in a law firm to shaping the next generation of AI. You will help define what excellent legal work looks like, test where our models meet that standard, and turn your findings into better model behavior and product experiences.

This is a hands-on individual contributor role at the intersection of legal practice and AI development. You will work directly with legal materials, model outputs, evaluation rubrics, and product prototypes. Your expertise will help us tackle some of the hardest questions in legal AI, including how to assess reasoning when there is no single correct answer.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.



In This Role, You Will:

 - Define the quality bar for what top-notch legal work looks like, drawing on real matters and the standards lawyers apply to research, analysis, drafting, document review, and client advice.

 - Design challenging, realistic AI model evaluations with representative facts, source materials, constraints, and deliverables, including cases that test ambiguity, competing arguments, and professional judgment.

 - Create and review reference work such as research memoranda, contract analyses, redlines, diligence findings, and draft legal documents that demonstrate strong reasoning and practical usefulness.

 - Develop rubrics that assess legal accuracy, issue spotting, factual grounding, citation validity, jurisdictional context, and the appropriate treatment of uncertainty.

 - Evaluate model outputs and complete legal workflows, identify recurring failures, and give researchers and engineers specific, actionable feedback supported by examples and corrected work.

 - Partner with Research on datasets, grading methods, and training tasks or environments that strengthen legal reasoning. Test whether model changes address the underlying problems and improve performance on new cases.

 - Work with Product and Engineering to identify valuable use cases, prototype workflows, and translate lessons from evaluations into experiences that fit how lawyers actually work.

 - Collaborate with legal professionals and design partners to refine our standards and test usefulness in practice, applying sound judgment around confidentiality, privilege, data permissions, and professional responsibility.



You Might Thrive in This Role If You:

 - Have practiced law at a law firm, with substantial experience producing and reviewing work for real client matters. We care more about demonstrated judgment and quality of work matter over title or firm pedigree.

 - Bring deep expertise in one or more practice areas, such as commercial transactions, corporate law, litigation, or regulatory work, and curiosity about workflows beyond your specialty.

 - Are an excellent legal researcher and writer who can assess authorities, distinguish strong arguments from plausible ones, and explain how facts and context affect a conclusion.

 - Can make expert judgment explicit: explain why an answer is incomplete, a clause creates risk, or an analysis misses the central issue, and describe what better work would look like.

 - Enjoy working directly with AI tools, exploring their limits, and testing ideas systematically. You can collaborate closely with technical teams and communicate clearly across disciplines.

 - Take ownership in ambiguous settings and are willing to build the first version of an evaluation, reference document, rubric, or workflow, then improve it through feedback.

 - Care deeply about the quality and consequences of legal work, and are motivated by the opportunity to help shape how AI supports the profession.



Especially Strong Candidates May Also Have:

 - Experience designing evaluations, benchmarks, datasets, or review frameworks for legal work or frontier AI systems.

 - A track record of improving legal workflows through technology, knowledge management, automation, or new ways of working.

 - Experience training or supervising lawyers, developing practice guidance, or translating complex legal concepts for different audiences.

You will own complex steering system and component decisions, define and cascade technical requirements, lead cross-functional execution, and serve as a trusted technical escalation point for steering design, validation, supplier, and production issues. Your scope may include steering columns, intermediate shafts, dash seals, electric power-assisted steering racks and gears, tie rods, fasteners, and next-generation mechatronic systems such as steer-by-wire, rear-wheel steering, and advanced ADAS steering technologies. The Expeditor is responsible for accelerating the flow of materials, components, and job orders through the manufacturing process to support on-time production and delivery. Monitor and expedite material, component, and job-order flow through all stages of manufacturing, including receiving, inspection, outside processing, fabrication, storage, and point-of-use delivery.
Review prioritized shortage and stalled-job queues daily, beginning with line-down, near-term production, and customer-delivery risks.
Verify material status and location using ERP records, transaction history, production schedules, inventory reports, and direct physical follow-up.
Identify the specific blocker preventing flow, including supplier delay, receiving, inspection, transportation, outside processing, fabrication, inventory discrepancy, transaction error, quality hold, or unclear ownership.
Coordinate the next required action with Production, Planning, Logistics, Procurement, Quality, and Shipping/Receiving, and escalate unresolved barriers through the appropriate leadership path.

Maintain accurate, current records in Oracle or other designated ERP and shortage-management tools, including owner, priority, due date, blocker, current status, and final disposition.
Identify recurring shortages, bottlenecks, aged queues, and repeated material movement failures; communicate trends and support root-cause and countermeasure activity.
Support continuous improvement and standard-work development that reduces reactive expediting, improves transactional discipline, and strengthens end-to-end material flow.

description:
Who we are

About the team
The Transaction Risk team builds the machine learning systems behind Stripe Radar, helping businesses prevent fraud and abuse while letting legitimate customers through. We combine intelligence from across Stripe’s global network with real-time models and AI agents to protect businesses across the customer lifecycle, from signup and free trials to payments and ongoing usage, with a growing focus on the emerging threats facing AI companies.
The team is growing, and expanding into multiple new areas. We are building abuse protections across the full customer life-cycle and solving emerging token fraud problems to make Stripe the default fraud and abuse solution for AI.
What you’ll do
You will own major ML systems and initiatives from problem definition to production. You'll find where ML can make the biggest difference, design the approach, build and ship models and the systems around them, and keep improving them as data, users, and attackers change.
Your work may include protecting businesses from abuse across the customer lifecycle, building adaptive and customizable fraud systems for Stripe's largest users, or extending risk intelligence to 50+ global payment methods. Across all of these, you'll use modern approaches, such as transformer models over payment data, graph intelligence across consumers, and LLMs that detect emerging attacks.
You will have opportunities to ship 0→1 products, and to improve mission-critical ML models operating at Stripe scale, often driving several efforts in parallel and setting the technical bar for the team.
Responsibilities
Lead the design and delivery of ML projects end to end, from framing the problem and sizing the opportunity through deployment, monitoring, and iteration.
Build, train, evaluate, and deploy models that detect fraud and abuse across Stripe’s global network, and own the production systems they run on.
Investigate emerging fraud and abuse patterns, decide where ML can have the most impact, and quickly turn those insights into shipped protections.
Design features, datasets, and evaluation strategies for noisy, delayed, and adversarial environments, and set the bar for experimental rigor.
Make sound architecture and modeling tradeoffs between model quality, legitimate-user impact, latency, reliability, and operational cost.
Be the go-to expert for the systems you own: lead incident response for model regressions, reduce operational toil, and make your systems easy for others to build on.
Partner with engineering, product, data science, risk experts, and leading Stripe users to turn modeling improvements into differentiated Radar products.
Turn recurring problems into reusable components, tools, and AI-assisted workflows that speed up the whole team.
Mentor engineers, give thoughtful design and code reviews, and help new teammates ramp up quickly.
Who you are
You are an experienced ML engineer who combines deep modeling expertise with strong engineering judgment. You've owned ML systems in production, shipped multiple meaningful improvements, and made the people around you more effective. You move fast without breaking things, you're comfortable leading through ambiguity, and you're excited to work at the frontier of payments and AI, turning advances in machine learning into production systems that address new forms of fraud and abuse.

5+ years of experience developing, evaluating, and deploying machine learning models in a production environment.
A track record of leading ML projects from problem definition to production, with measurable impact.
Deep foundations in machine learning, statistics, model evaluation, and experiment design.
Strong programming and software-engineering skills, with experience writing tested, maintainable code for production ML applications.
Experience designing and operating production ML systems, including several of: large-scale data and feature pipelines, distributed model training, low-latency inference, model deployment, or production monitoring.
Experience mentoring engineers or technically leading projects with multiple contributors.
Ability to investigate ambiguous problems, reason from data, and choose pragmatic technical approaches.
Ability to communicate technical ideas and results clearly and collaborate effectively across disciplines.

Experience applying ML to fraud detection, integrity, trust and safety, identity, cybersecurity, or another adversarial domain.
Experience developing or productionizing modern deep learning, graph-learning, or LLM-based approaches.
Experience building and optimizing real-time, low-latency ML systems at scale.

Experience rapidly building 0→1 products or working directly with customers.
Experience building AI-assisted tooling or agents that measurably increased a team's velocity.

Excellent communication skills with technical buyers (engineers, product managers, technical founders)

Experience as a software engineer, product manager, or in other technical roles.

Familiarity and enthusiasm for AI developer tooling (Cursor, Lovable, Vercel, LangChain, etc.) and the broader AI infrastructure ecosystem

title: Regulatory Operations Associate
description:
Via is using technology to transform transportation around the world. From changing a single person’s daily commute to reducing humanity’s collective environmental footprint — we’ve got huge goals.
As a Regulatory Operations Associate , you will handle the day-to-day execution, tracking, and operational tasks required to keep Via’s transit partnerships fully compliant. You will monitor operational workflows, maintain audit-ready documentation, coordinate filings, and support the rollout of internal tools and automated reporting systems across our partner deployments.
This role is based in NYC with a 3x per week office requirement.
What You’ll Do
Daily Compliance Execution: Coordinate and submit recurring regulatory filings, vehicle permits, driver credential verifications, and operational reports required by local transit agencies, federal standards (FTA), and accessibility mandates (ADA).
Audit & Records Maintenance: Maintain centralized documentation systems, log compliance records, and perform routine audits of service data to ensure all partner markets remain 100% audit-ready.
Tooling & Data Entry Workflows: Utilize internal operational tools, AI-assisted reporting workflows, and databases to extract compliance metrics, log discrepancies, and replace manual paperwork with structured digital tracking.
Operational Monitoring: Track day-to-day Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and incident reports, flagging non-compliance issues or emerging operational bottlenecks directly to market operations managers.
Project Coordination: Update and maintain project trackers, compliance calendars, and operational checklists to ensure all milestone dates, renewals, and partner deliverables are completed on schedule.
Cross-Functional Support: Liaise directly with local Fleet Coordinators, Dispatch, Legal, and Market Operations teams to gather evidence, verify on-the-ground operational facts, and resolve administrative compliance blockers.
Who You Are
1–3 years of professional experience in operations, compliance coordination, program administration, logistics, or a related task-focused operational role; Bachelor's degree required.
Highly organized task manager who thrives on executing recurring workflows accurately and keeping structured trackers up to date.
Meticulous attention to detail with a track record of verifying datasets, maintaining clean records, and spotting discrepancies in operational data.
Clear, practical communicator able to coordinate across frontline operations, legal, and city teams to track down required documentation.
Fast learner comfortable adopting new software platforms, spreadsheets, and internal workflow tools quickly.
Prior experience with Salesforce, Google Sheets/Excel, or compliance tracking software is a plus, but not required.

Final salary will be determined by the candidate’s experience, knowledge, and skills. Salary reflected does not include equity or variable pay, where applicable.

title: Senior Facilities Engineer
location: United States of America - Colorado - Denver
description:

Job Description:
bpx energy, a major oil and gas producer in the United States, leverages its expertise in unconventional gas, including shale, to deliver hydrocarbon production and technical knowledge worldwide. With operations in Texas and Louisiana, our US onshore business has become both a premier oil and gas producer and a leader in reducing methane emissions.
As part of BP, a global industry leader, we foster a high-energy, high-intensity environment built on accountability, collegiality, innovation, and empowerment. At bpx, we support our people to learn and grow in a diverse and challenging environment where collaboration, continuous improvement, and inclusion are valued.
Discover your place with us and help our business meet the challenges of reimagining and reinventing the future of energy.
Role Synopsis
We are seeking a highly motivated individual who enjoys a dynamic work environment. This role is responsible for contributing to the facilities engineering team in the bpx Eagle Ford Basin to deliver strategic initiatives on process safety, production & reliability optimization, and sustainable emissions reductions. This individual must proactively interact with other disciplines, teams, subfunctions and contractors to systematically resolve problems. Core competencies of this role include applying sound engineering judgement to drive integrated, pragmatic solutions focused on facility reliability, defect elimination, risk management, operating efficiency, and emissions improvement.
Key Accountabilities
Provide brownfield project-level and rapid response engineering for facility modifications, focusing on strategic initiatives such as surface artificial lift, compression optimization, and facility retrofits.
Design surface facilities such as compression systems, control valves, piping, storage tanks, combustors, and pressure relief systems to optimize process safety and well pad production.
Initiate and coordinate Management of Change (MOC) processes for facility modifications, including work packs, P&IDs, cause-and-effect diagrams, and plot plans.
Lead design reviews and risk assessments inclusive of HAZOP / What If studies to eliminate personal and process safety risks through effective implementation of the hierarchy of controls.
Lead project management of engineered solutions, including economic analysis, cost management, and post-implementation appraisals.
Analyze material release data, perform Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA), and execute corrective actions and projects to reduce failures and associated costs.
Lead defect elimination, and reliability improvement initiatives in collaboration with maintenance and operations team to minimize down time.
Manage and optimize chemical treatment, integrity management and specialty / safety critical equipment programs.
Manage and oversee service providers (e.g., engineering, compression, chemical, etc.) to ensure compliance with established safety and performance KPIs.
Embrace a positive culture of collaboration by sharing lessons learned across disciplines and between business functions.
Participate in BP technical networks and communities of practice, maintaining a strong awareness of technical learnings and developing links with specialists and engineers from a range of disciplines.
Follow BP's Engineering Principles, comply with BP's Code of Conduct, and model BP's Values & Behaviors.
Essential Experience and Education
Bachelor’s degree in petroleum, chemical, or mechanical engineering
5-7 years minimum experience in US onshore operations / facility engineering.
Working knowledge of the following:
PFDs, P&IDs, and Cause & Effect Diagrams.
Piping codes (either ASME 31.3 or 31.8) and ASME pressure vessel code.
Reciprocal compressor sizing, separator sizing, pressure relief design, and tank vent calculations.
API 12F tank specification.
Proven ability to manage multiple projects and prioritize tasks effectively.
Familiarity in implementing and managing process safety management systems.
Hands-on experience facilitating Process Hazard Analysis (PHA) sessions (HAZOP and/or What-If studies)
Experience driving contractor accountability and implementing corrective actions to meet established KPIs.
Ability to analyze complex data sets, identify patterns and anomalies, and apply engineering principles to troubleshoot issues and optimize systems.
Familiarity with RCFA to identify issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurring failures.
Practical knowledge of artificial lift systems (gas lift, rod pump, plunger lift, etc.).

Interpersonal Skills:
Motivated, self-starter enthusiastic about affecting change to drive upstream innovation.
Ability to collaborate and build alignment with individuals and within multi-discipline teams.
Proficient in clearly and confidently presenting complex technical issues to a wide range of audiences.
Growth mindset: proven ability to quickly learn new concepts, processes, software, engineering and mathematically ideas.

Pneumatic, electrical controls and safety system design knowledge.
Experience with Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA).
Familiarity with integrity management processes (NDE/NDT).
Knowledge of metallurgy, welding types and welding procedures.
Understanding of NACE standards for corrosion control and materials selection.
Proficiency in AutoCAD and/or Bluebeam.
Process modeling experience with ProMax or similar software.
